references: Joy Ang: Moon Rising cover and official NightWing tribe drawing
Brianna C. Walsh: official How to Draw Moon and Starflight
Mike Holmes: Starflight frontal/dorsal oblique and Morrowseer frontal oblique, Scholastic Dark Secret preview pages 11 and 24

head.why: Joy Ang NightWing/How to Draw anatomy is the primary muzzle source: tapered nasal wedge and an overhanging beaked tip, retaining broad underlying cranial support. Graphic novel facial compression is not the nose template.

cranial_vault.why: Posterior cranial roof is independent of the orbital rim, continuing into the occiput and arched upper cervical attachment.

body.why: Clay-derived full trunk and named muscle profiles with a NightWing S-curve cervical centerline: forward lower neck, recessed mid-cervical bend, upper arch and a near-horizontal approach into the skull base. Actual rig stations follow those spinal landmarks.
body.upper_neck_fit: Relaxed cranial return: no dorsal centerline hump above the occipital station; longer fore-aft transition into the skull.

horn.why: User reference: the skull grows into a housing over the horn root. Almost straight swept shafts with a very slight upward arch and distinct satin grey keratin; no exposed end caps or downward-curled tips.

wing.why: Longer humeral/forearm segments account for side-reference foreshortening. Outer flight rays extend the spread span; body-side rays shorten. Contracted rays remain ordered and close, with the pointer lower than the second ray to create an arc. Clay-derived humeral, forearm and carpal anatomy supports continuous membranes.

physical_estimate.status: inferred game scale, not canon dimensions
physical_estimate.method: Age and small/strong-muscled descriptions constrain relative scale against the established Clay/human world. Export measures actual geometry and estimates mass from the closed primary body plus head/jaw volume, allowing 10% head-neck overlap. Effective density is an explicit speculative biological assumption, not a book fact.
physical_estimate.maturity_basis: Rapid growth through roughly seven years; four-year-old Moon is modeled as an advanced juvenile, not at 4/7 adult linear size. The 83% size choice is an explicit interpolation, not a published age-to-height equation.

mouth.why: Final upper host and matching lower jaw share the bite boundary. Clay tooth primitive, curved front/side gum arches, surface-seated roots and floor-referenced tongue replace quantile placement and fixed coordinates.

eye.why: Lateral equine-like orbital orientation, retaining NightWing green iris and vertical pupil; fitted source globe, host and staged lids remain one seated assembly.

nose_cap.why: Short terminal cap follows the bounded colored reference: a local eagle-like premaxillary tip rather than a long gray sleeve. Curved dorsal boundary and two recessed nostril apertures.
